---
title: Retrying & Logging
---

Search-agent runs combine several independent services and long-lived tasks.
Reliable operation depends on bounding each failure domain and preserving enough
evidence to resume or diagnose a run.

### Retry at the correct boundary

SearcherKit has separate retry scopes:

| Scope | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| LLM retry | Transient provider failures or recoverable parse failures |
| Tool retry | Temporary source, MCP, or tool failures |
| Task retry | Restarting an entire trajectory |

Only list exceptions that are genuinely recoverable. Authentication errors,
invalid model names, malformed permanent config, and deterministic schema
errors should surface immediately. Test both eventual success and exhausted
retry behavior.

### Bound agent execution

Configure turn, token, and time budgets together. Reminder prompts near those
limits should tell the model to stop using tools and produce the required final
answer format. A caller may still enforce a hard timeout around the whole run.

### Preserve observability

For production-scale runs, keep:

- a global log for lifecycle and aggregate failures;
- one trace log per trajectory;
- structured message histories and timing data;
- checkpoint state and a run summary;
- model, dataset, config, and code revisions outside the output directory.

Avoid logging secrets or complete credentials. Prefer stable sample and trace
identifiers so a summary failure can be followed into the relevant history and
trace.

### Diagnose in layers

1. Run `searcher inspect` to rule out config shape errors.
2. Use `searcher tui` or a one-item dataset to test one trajectory.
3. Check model and retrieval services independently.
4. Read the per-trace log to identify the failing boundary.
5. Increase concurrency gradually while watching queue depth, latency, retries,
   and failure rate.

For batch regressions, separate task completion from answer quality. A run can
complete successfully while producing invalid tool calls, repeated searches,
truncated context, or an answer format the evaluator cannot extract.
